subject: English
chapter: Grammar: Clauses (Noun, Adjective and Adverb Clauses)
central_question: How can a student identify and use noun, adjective and adverb clauses according to the grammatical function each clause performs?
in_scope_units: Clause, independent clause and dependent clause
Noun clauses as subject, object or complement
Adjective or relative clauses describing nouns
Adverb clauses of time, place, reason, condition, purpose and contrast
Common clause errors including misclassification, missing subordinators and comma splices

known_pitfalls.claim: Calling every clause beginning with that a noun clause.
known_pitfalls.correction: Classify by function; if the clause describes a noun, it is an adjective clause.

known_pitfalls.claim: Writing an incomplete subordinate structure such as "He said he honest."
known_pitfalls.correction: Use a complete clause with subject and verb, for example "He said that he was honest."

known_pitfalls.claim: Joining two independent clauses with only a comma.
known_pitfalls.correction: Use a conjunction or make one clause subordinate.

recommended_example_progression: Combine ideas with adverb clauses of reason, purpose or contrast
Classify mixed clauses and correct comma splices
ncert_end_of_chapter_exercises_reference: Typical CBSE practice includes identifying clause types, combining sentences with suitable clauses, completing subordinate clauses, and correcting clause or punctuation errors.
